$comment: Issue #468 — the owner-controlled RFC 9116 policy behind GET /.well-known/security.txt. The document is rendered from THIS file only (src/http/security-txt/), validated by SecurityTxtManifestSchema, and served ONLY while approval.status is 'approved'. It is 'pending' today: this repository publishes no vulnerability-reporting address (src/contact/channels.json deliberately lists no address, and docs/security.md routes urgent reports through an operator channel that is not public), so there is nothing to publish that is not a guess. To approve: (1) add at least one Contact the operator actually monitors, (2) set approval.status to 'approved' with approval.approved_at / approval.approved_by, (3) re-run `pnpm exec vitest run src/http/security-txt` — the gate flips from 404 to 200 on its own. DO NOT add an address the operator has not published and stands behind: a security.txt is read by strangers and by scanners, and a dead or unmonitored mailbox is a worse outcome than the 404 this file currently produces.

approval.note: Awaiting an owner decision on the reporting channel (Issue #468: 連絡可能な脆弱性報告窓口、対象、expiresをowner承認後にsecurity.txtとして配信). Nothing about the delivery mechanism is blocked — the renderer, the RFC 9116 §6 field grammar, the expiry gate, the HTTP contract and the browser screenshot are all complete and proven over a local fixture; only the human answer is missing.
